title: Third-engine candidate: Z80 Atlas (byte-level heredity) adapter contract + known-answer smoke test (s11)
objective: A concrete adapter contract (or a documented incompatibility) for a byte-level hereditary runtime, plus a known-answer smoke test.
problem: Read-only against the Z80 Atlas lane. Question to PREPARE, not run: can a heritable computational structure transmit a functional capability across generations, and can the Observatory tell inheritance from environmental reconstruction or seeded copying? Deliver: owner, pinned SHA, entry points, generation-boundary semantics, what inheritance / reconstruction / seeded-copy controls would look like natively, which registry entries could apply, and a known-answer smoke test (a planted heritable program is transmitted and detected; a non-heritable one is not) in the RSO lane against the pinned code. No large experiment.
non_goals: No edit in the Z80 Atlas lane
No edit in another seat's lane
evidence_required: smoke test committed with its command and result

acceptance.condition: all evidence_required items; committed with source references
